source: SRJ editorial profiles, written from durable public knowledge
caveat: Pricing, version numbers, context-window sizes, and compliance certifications change frequently. Where stated they are accurate as of the as_of date and should be confirmed with the vendor before any procurement or compliance decision. Where they could not be stated confidently they are omitted rather than guessed.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.tagline: The general-purpose assistant that made conversational AI a business tool.
chatgpt.value: The broadest general-purpose assistant available, and the default most organizations encounter first. Its advantage is coverage rather than any single capability: text, code, images, voice, file analysis, and web browsing in one place, with the largest ecosystem of third-party familiarity around it.
use_cases: Drafting and revising business writing, from board memos to customer email
Ad-hoc analysis of uploaded spreadsheets and documents without building a pipeline
Prototyping and debugging code, including for people who are not primarily developers
chatgpt.engine: OpenAI's proprietary GPT model family. Not open weight.
chatgpt.files: Accepts documents, spreadsheets, images, and code files in the paid tiers. Long context, though the exact window varies by model tier and changes frequently.
chatgpt.latency: Fast on the standard models. Reasoning-oriented models trade noticeably longer response times for better multi-step work.
chatgpt.quality: Strong general fluency and broad world knowledge. Like all LLMs it will state incorrect facts confidently, and it is weakest on recent events, niche technical detail, and anything requiring precise citation.

pricing.limits: Message caps, limited access to newer models

pricing.includes: Priority access, advanced models, higher limits
Admin controls, SSO, workspace data controls

chatgpt.training_optout: Configurable. Business and enterprise tiers are not used to train models by default; consumer tiers require changing a setting. Verify the current terms for your specific tier before putting regulated data through it.
chatgpt.governance_note: The consumer-versus-business distinction here is the single most common AI governance gap found in practice: staff use the free tier with company data under different terms than the enterprise agreement legal reviewed.
integrations: Direct connectors to common storage and productivity suites
chatgpt.api: REST API with official Python and TypeScript SDKs. Widely supported by every major orchestration framework.
pros: Broadest capability coverage in one product
Largest ecosystem and integration surface
Strong at the general business writing and analysis most staff actually need
cons: Consumer and enterprise data terms differ, which is a real governance trap
Model behaviour and limits change without much notice
Not the strongest at long-document reasoning or coding fidelity

claude.name: Claude
claude.tagline: The assistant most often chosen for long-document work and writing quality.
claude.value: Strongest of the general assistants at sustained reasoning over long documents and at producing prose that does not need heavy editing. Frequently the choice where the input is a contract, a filing, or a full codebase rather than a short prompt.
use_cases: Reviewing long contracts, policies, and regulatory filings in a single pass
Drafting substantial written work where tone and structure matter
Codebase-level engineering work rather than snippet completion
claude.engine: Anthropic's proprietary Claude model family. Not open weight.
claude.files: Accepts documents, spreadsheets, images, and code. Large context window, which is the specific reason it is chosen for long-document work.
claude.latency: Comparable to peers on standard models. Extended-reasoning modes are markedly slower and markedly better on hard multi-step problems.
claude.quality: Notably strong at instruction-following, long-context retrieval, and writing that reads as intended. Still subject to confident error, and like all LLMs should not be trusted for citations without checking them.

pricing.includes: Higher limits, priority access, advanced models
Direct model access, batch and caching options

claude.training_optout: Anthropic does not train its models on business or API customer data by default. Confirm the terms attached to your specific plan.
integrations: Model Context Protocol connectors to third-party systems
Available through major cloud model marketplaces
claude.api: REST API with official SDKs. Also distributed through major cloud providers, which matters for organizations that need the data to stay inside an existing cloud agreement.
pros: Best-in-class long-document reasoning
Writing quality needs the least editing
Strong safety posture and clear enterprise data terms
cons: Smaller third-party app ecosystem than OpenAI's
Usage caps on consumer tiers bite quickly under heavy use
Fewer built-in modalities, with image generation notably absent

gemini.name: Gemini
gemini.tagline: Google's assistant, strongest where the work already lives in Google Workspace.
gemini.value: The most natural choice for organizations already standardised on Google Workspace, because it reaches directly into Docs, Sheets, Gmail, and Drive rather than requiring content to be pasted into a separate tool.
use_cases: Summarising and drafting inside Gmail, Docs, and Sheets without leaving them
Analysing very large documents and long video or audio inputs
Building on Google Cloud through Vertex AI with existing IAM and data residency controls
gemini.engine: Google's proprietary Gemini model family. Not open weight.
gemini.files: Broad multimodal input including text, images, audio, and video. Very large context windows on the higher tiers, which is one of its genuine differentiators.
gemini.latency: Fast on the lighter models, slower on the largest. Generally competitive.
gemini.quality: Strong multimodal handling and very long context. Quality across text tasks is competitive but not consistently ahead of its peers.

pricing.includes: Advanced models, larger limits, storage bundle
In-app AI across Workspace, admin controls

gemini.training_optout: Enterprise Workspace and Vertex AI customer data is not used to train models. Consumer terms differ. As with ChatGPT, the tier distinction is where governance problems start.
gemini.api: REST API and SDKs, plus Vertex AI for enterprise deployment with cloud-native controls.
pros: Deepest Workspace integration of any assistant
Very large context windows
Enterprise controls and data residency through Vertex AI
cons: Product naming and tiering are genuinely confusing
Quality less consistent than its top peers on hard text tasks
Best value depends on already being a Google shop

microsoft-copilot.name: Microsoft Copilot
microsoft-copilot.tagline: AI embedded in Microsoft 365, where most enterprise work already happens.
microsoft-copilot.value: Reaches into Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint with the organization's own content, under existing Microsoft tenancy, identity, and compliance controls. For most large enterprises that governance continuity matters more than raw model quality.
use_cases: Summarising Teams meetings and long Outlook threads
Drafting and analysing directly inside Word and Excel against internal documents
Surfacing answers from SharePoint and internal knowledge under existing permissions
microsoft-copilot.engine: Primarily OpenAI models running under Microsoft's enterprise infrastructure, with Microsoft's own models in some surfaces.
microsoft-copilot.files: Works against the organization's existing Microsoft 365 content, which is the point. Standard document and spreadsheet handling.
microsoft-copilot.latency: Adequate. Perceived speed varies considerably by host application.
microsoft-copilot.quality: Model quality is competitive. The differentiator is grounding in the tenant's own data with permissions respected, not standalone reasoning.

pricing.includes: In-app AI across Microsoft 365, tenant grounding, admin controls
Direct model access under Azure controls

microsoft-copilot.training_optout: Commercial data protection applies to licensed enterprise use: prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models. The free consumer tier operates under different terms.
microsoft-copilot.governance_note: Because it inherits existing Microsoft 365 permissions, it will surface anything a user already had access to. Organizations with permissive legacy SharePoint permissions frequently discover the problem only after deployment. Fix permissions before rollout, not after.
microsoft-copilot.api: Available through Azure OpenAI for direct model access, and extensible via Copilot Studio.
pros: Governance and identity continuity with existing Microsoft tenancy
Grounded in the organization's own content
Easiest enterprise procurement path for Microsoft shops
cons: Expensive per seat, and value varies widely by role
Exposes pre-existing permission sprawl
Quality inconsistent across host applications

github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
github-copilot.tagline: The most widely deployed AI coding assistant, and the default in most enterprises.
github-copilot.value: The safest institutional choice for AI-assisted coding: broad IDE support, mature enterprise administration, and an established procurement path. Rarely the most capable option, usually the easiest to approve.
use_cases: Inline code completion across the editors teams already use
Generating unit tests and boilerplate
Explaining unfamiliar code and assisting review
github-copilot.engine: Multiple underlying models, primarily OpenAI, with other model options in some tiers.
github-copilot.files: Works against the open repository and editor context. Repository-wide awareness varies by tier and editor.
github-copilot.latency: Low latency for completion, which is the property that matters most for inline use.
github-copilot.quality: Strong at idiomatic completion and boilerplate. Weaker at large multi-file refactors, where dedicated agentic tools have moved ahead.

pricing.includes: Policy controls, audit logs, IP indemnity

github-copilot.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers exclude customer code from model training. A public-code filter is available. Confirm current terms for your tier.
github-copilot.governance_note: The enterprise tiers carry IP indemnity for suggestions, which is usually the deciding factor for legal review rather than any capability difference.
integrations: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim
github-copilot.api: Not a general-purpose API product. Extensibility is through editor extensions and GitHub.
pros: Broadest IDE coverage
Mature enterprise administration and audit
IP indemnity on business tiers
cons: Behind dedicated agentic editors on large refactors
Premium request caps can surprise heavy users
Quality varies by language and by editor

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.tagline: An AI-first code editor built around whole-codebase work rather than autocomplete.
cursor.value: A full editor rather than a plugin, which lets it reason across an entire codebase and apply multi-file changes. Where Copilot completes the line you are typing, Cursor is aimed at the change you are trying to make.
use_cases: Multi-file refactors and feature work across a large repository
Understanding an unfamiliar codebase quickly
Agentic tasks where the tool edits, runs, and iterates
cursor.engine: Model-agnostic. Routes to frontier models from multiple vendors, with its own models for fast completion.
cursor.files: Full repository context with its own indexing, which is the core of the product.
cursor.latency: Fast for completion. Agentic multi-file work is necessarily slower.
cursor.quality: Among the strongest available for substantial code changes. Agentic edits still need genuine review, and confident wrong changes across several files are harder to catch than a single bad line.

pricing.includes: Privacy mode enforcement, SSO, admin controls

cursor.training_optout: A privacy mode prevents code being retained, and business tiers can enforce it across the organization. Verify current terms before regulated code goes near it.
cursor.governance_note: Because it routes to multiple third-party model providers, the data path is worth mapping explicitly during vendor review. It is not a single-vendor relationship even though it is a single purchase.
integrations: Forked from VS Code, so most VS Code extensions work
cursor.api: No general API. It is an editor, not a platform.
pros: Best-in-class whole-codebase and multi-file work
Model choice rather than lock-in
Familiar to any VS Code user immediately
cons: Requires replacing the editor, not adding to it
Usage pricing can escalate unpredictably
Multi-vendor data path complicates vendor review

perplexity-ai.name: Perplexity AI
perplexity-ai.tagline: Search rebuilt as a citing answer engine rather than a list of links.
perplexity-ai.value: Answers questions with inline citations to the sources used, which makes it materially more checkable than a general assistant. The right tool when the answer needs to be traced back rather than merely produced.
use_cases: Fast market and competitor research with sources attached
Checking a current fact where a general model's knowledge would be stale
First-pass literature and regulatory scanning before deeper verification
perplexity-ai.engine: Model-agnostic, routing to frontier models from several vendors, layered over its own retrieval and ranking.
perplexity-ai.files: Accepts document uploads on paid tiers, with web retrieval as the primary input.
perplexity-ai.quality: Citations are the differentiator and the caveat. They make verification possible, but a citation is not a guarantee: the tool sometimes cites a source that does not fully support the sentence. Read the source, do not trust the footnote.

pricing.includes: Advanced model choice, file upload, higher limits
SSO, admin controls, data retention controls

perplexity-ai.training_optout: Enterprise tiers offer data controls and an AI training opt-out. Consumer tiers differ. Verify before regulated research goes through it.
perplexity-ai.governance_note: For an audit or compliance workflow, treat its citations exactly as this site treats news: a lead to the primary source, never the evidence itself.
perplexity-ai.api: REST API returning answers with source citations.
pros: Citations make answers checkable
Genuinely current, unlike static model knowledge
Model choice rather than lock-in
cons: A citation does not always support the claim attached to it
Weaker than dedicated assistants at writing and reasoning
Source quality varies with what ranks well

hugging-face.name: Hugging Face
hugging-face.tagline: The public infrastructure of open-weight AI: models, datasets, and the libraries around them.
hugging-face.value: Where open-weight models and their datasets actually live. Less a product than the distribution layer the entire open-model ecosystem depends on, including the tooling most teams use to run models themselves.
use_cases: Finding, comparing, and downloading open-weight models for self-hosting
Building on the Transformers library rather than a vendor API
Sourcing and publishing datasets, and reading model cards before adopting a model
hugging-face.engine: Not a model itself. A hub and a set of libraries hosting models from many publishers.
hugging-face.files: Hosts model weights, datasets, and demo applications.
hugging-face.latency: Not applicable to the hub. Hosted inference performance depends on the model and tier.
hugging-face.quality: Quality varies enormously by publisher, which is the nature of an open hub. Model cards and licences must be read individually.

pricing.includes: Public model and dataset access, community features
SSO, audit logs, access controls, region selection

hugging-face.training_optout: Self-hosted use means data never leaves the organization, which is the main governance argument for open weights in the first place.
hugging-face.governance_note: The critical governance step here is licence review. Open weight does not mean open licence, and several widely used models carry commercial restrictions or acceptable-use terms that survive fine-tuning. Read the licence, not the headline.
hugging-face.api: REST inference API plus the Python libraries that are the de facto standard for working with open models.
pros: The definitive source for open-weight models
Self-hosting removes third-party data exposure entirely
Model cards support genuine due diligence
cons: Quality and licensing vary wildly by publisher
Self-hosting shifts the entire operational burden in-house
Requires real ML engineering capability

llama-meta.name: Llama (Meta)
llama-meta.tagline: The most widely adopted open-weight model family, and the usual starting point for self-hosting.
llama-meta.value: Removes the third-party data path entirely: weights can be run on infrastructure the organization controls. For regulated environments that is frequently the deciding factor, irrespective of benchmark position.
use_cases: Running a capable model entirely inside a controlled environment
Fine-tuning on proprietary data without sending it to a vendor
Avoiding per-token costs at high, predictable volume
llama-meta.engine: Meta's own open-weight model family, released in several sizes.
llama-meta.files: Depends entirely on the serving stack chosen, not on the model distribution.
llama-meta.latency: A function of the hardware it runs on. Smaller variants run acceptably on modest hardware; the largest need serious GPU capacity.
llama-meta.quality: Competitive with proprietary models on many tasks, generally behind the frontier ones on the hardest reasoning. The trade is capability for control.

pricing.includes: Full weights, fine-tuning rights subject to licence
Managed inference from cloud and inference providers

llama-meta.training_optout: Not applicable when self-hosted: the data never leaves your environment. That is the entire argument for this option.
llama-meta.governance_note: The licence is a community licence, not a standard open-source licence. It carries conditions, including at very large user scale. Have counsel read it before building a commercial product on it rather than assuming MIT-style terms.
llama-meta.api: No first-party API. Served through whatever stack you choose or a third-party host.
pros: Complete data control when self-hosted
No per-token cost at volume
Large ecosystem and abundant tooling
cons: Community licence is not standard open source and has real conditions
Behind the frontier on hardest reasoning
Self-hosting demands infrastructure and ML capability

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.tagline: The quality leader in synthetic speech, and a live example of why voice needs governance.
elevenlabs.value: Produces synthetic speech convincing enough for commercial publication, with multilingual output and voice cloning from short samples. The realism is the product and the risk in equal measure.
use_cases: Narration for training, marketing, and product content at scale
Dubbing existing content into other languages while keeping the speaker's voice
Accessibility, turning written material into audio
elevenlabs.engine: Proprietary speech synthesis and voice cloning models.
elevenlabs.files: Text in, audio out. Accepts reference audio for cloning and existing media for dubbing.
elevenlabs.latency: Fast enough for near real-time use in the low-latency modes.
elevenlabs.quality: The realism benchmark for the category. Long-form prosody and unusual proper nouns remain the weak points.
elevenlabs.training_optout: Enterprise agreements address data use. Verify terms before uploading any voice you do not own.
elevenlabs.governance_note: This is the tool most likely to create legal exposure through ordinary use. Cloning a voice requires the speaker's consent, several jurisdictions now regulate synthetic likeness directly, and Tennessee's ELVIS Act is one example already covered in the governance library. Consent capture and provenance labelling belong in the workflow from day one, not after the first complaint.
elevenlabs.api: REST API with SDKs, including low-latency streaming.
pros: Best-in-class output realism
Strong multilingual and dubbing capability
Straightforward API
cons: Voice cloning carries real and rising legal exposure
Character-based pricing escalates with long-form use
Free tier prohibits commercial use, which is easy to miss

mistral-le-chat.name: Mistral / Le Chat
mistral-le-chat.tagline: The European frontier lab, and the usual answer when data must stay in the EU.
mistral-le-chat.value: A capable frontier model family from a European company, with several models released under open weights. For organizations whose constraint is where the data goes rather than which model scores highest, that combination is often decisive.
use_cases: Deploying a capable assistant where EU data residency is a hard requirement
Self-hosting an open-weight model with a genuinely permissive licence
Reducing dependence on a single US model vendor
mistral-le-chat.engine: Mistral's own model family. Several models are released under Apache 2.0; the largest are proprietary.
mistral-le-chat.files: Document and image handling on the hosted product. Self-hosted capability depends on the serving stack.
mistral-le-chat.latency: The smaller models are notably fast and cheap to run, which is a large part of their appeal for high-volume work.
mistral-le-chat.quality: Competitive, particularly for the size and cost. Generally behind the largest US frontier models on the hardest reasoning tasks.
mistral-le-chat.training_optout: Business and API terms address training use. Self-hosting removes the question entirely. Confirm the terms attached to your specific tier.
mistral-le-chat.governance_note: This is the clearest available answer to a GDPR transfer problem. Where a US vendor's data path forces a Chapter V transfer analysis, an EU-hosted or self-hosted European model avoids the question rather than mitigating it. Note the distinction between the Apache-licensed models and the proprietary ones, because only the former can actually be run on your own infrastructure.
integrations: Hugging Face, Ollama, and standard self-hosting stacks
mistral-le-chat.api: REST API with SDKs, plus open weights for the models released that way.
pros: Genuine EU alternative with real data residency options
Apache 2.0 on several capable models
Excellent cost and speed at the smaller sizes
cons: Behind the frontier on hardest reasoning
Smaller ecosystem than the US majors
Open and proprietary model split is easy to confuse

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.tagline: Frontier-class capability at very low cost, from a Chinese vendor, which is the whole governance story.
deepseek.value: Reasoning performance close to the frontier at a fraction of the cost, with open-weight releases. The capability is real. The governance considerations are equally real and are the reason it needs its own policy decision rather than a default allow.
use_cases: High-volume reasoning workloads where per-token cost dominates
Self-hosting an open-weight reasoning model on controlled infrastructure
Benchmarking against incumbents to test whether premium pricing is justified
deepseek.engine: DeepSeek's own models, with several released as open weights.
deepseek.files: Standard text and code handling on the hosted service.
deepseek.latency: Reasoning models trade latency for quality, as elsewhere in the category.
deepseek.quality: Genuinely strong at mathematics and code reasoning. Outputs reflect Chinese regulatory content requirements on politically sensitive subjects, which is a factual property of the model rather than a criticism.
deepseek.training_optout: The hosted service is operated from China and subject to Chinese law, including data access provisions. Self-hosting the open weights removes the data path entirely and is the only version most regulated organizations should consider.
deepseek.governance_note: Treat the hosted API and the open weights as two different decisions. The weights can be run on your own infrastructure with no data leaving; the hosted API sends prompts to servers under Chinese jurisdiction, which triggers cross-border transfer analysis, and in some sectors and government contexts an outright prohibition. Several jurisdictions have restricted it on government devices. See the China AI regulation and global AI laws pages in the reference library before approving either.
integrations: Hugging Face and standard self-hosting stacks
deepseek.api: REST API, largely OpenAI-compatible, which makes swapping it in unusually easy. That ease is itself a shadow-IT risk worth naming.
pros: Frontier-adjacent reasoning at very low cost
Open weights available for self-hosting
Drop-in API compatibility
cons: Hosted service sits under Chinese jurisdiction
Restricted on government devices in several jurisdictions
Content behaviour reflects Chinese regulatory requirements

ollama.name: Ollama
ollama.tagline: The simplest way to run open-weight models entirely on your own machine.
ollama.value: Turns self-hosting from an infrastructure project into a single install. Pulls and runs open-weight models locally with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which means existing code usually points at it unchanged.
use_cases: Running an assistant on confidential material with no network path at all
Local development against a model without per-token cost
Air-gapped or high-sensitivity environments where no external API is permitted
ollama.engine: Not a model. A runtime and model manager that serves open-weight models locally.
ollama.files: Depends on the model served. Text and, for multimodal models, images.
ollama.latency: Bounded entirely by local hardware. Small models are fast on a modern laptop; large ones need serious GPU capacity.
ollama.quality: Exactly the quality of whichever open-weight model is loaded. Ollama adds no capability and takes none away.

pricing.includes: Full local runtime and model library

ollama.training_optout: Not applicable. Nothing leaves the machine, which is the entire reason to use it.
ollama.governance_note: This is the strongest available answer to 'we cannot send this data anywhere'. It converts an AI vendor risk assessment into an endpoint security question, which most organizations already know how to run. The residual risks move to the model licence and to unmanaged installs on staff laptops, so pair adoption with a licence review and an endpoint policy.
ollama.api: Local REST API that is largely OpenAI-compatible, so most existing code can be repointed with a base-URL change.
pros: Data never leaves the machine
Trivial to install compared with raw self-hosting
No per-token cost
cons: Capability limited by local hardware
Model licences still apply and still need review
Easy for staff to install without oversight

midjourney.name: Midjourney
midjourney.tagline: The aesthetic leader in image generation, with the least clear commercial-use position.
midjourney.value: Consistently the strongest output aesthetics in the category. Chosen where the image has to look genuinely good rather than merely correct.
use_cases: Concept art, mood boards, and campaign visual exploration
Marketing imagery where style consistency matters
Rapid visual iteration before commissioning real production
midjourney.engine: Proprietary image models. Not open weight.
midjourney.files: Text prompts plus image references for style and composition control.
midjourney.latency: Seconds per generation, typically several variants at once.
midjourney.quality: Best-in-class aesthetics. Weaker than peers at rendering legible text in images and at precise, literal instruction-following.

pricing.includes: More fast time, relaxed unlimited generation
Highest quotas, stealth mode on upper tiers

midjourney.training_optout: Generations are public by default on lower tiers. Private generation requires an upper tier. That default alone disqualifies it for confidential product work unless the tier is chosen deliberately.
midjourney.governance_note: Two live issues. First, the public-by-default behaviour: staff experimenting with an unreleased product name or design are publishing it. Second, the training-data provenance question that image generators face collectively, which is the subject of ongoing litigation and which Midjourney has not resolved through licensing the way Adobe has. Where indemnity matters more than aesthetics, Firefly is the safer choice, and the reference library's copyright material is the place to start.
midjourney.api: No official public API. Automation depends on unofficial routes, which carry their own terms-of-service risk.
pros: Best output aesthetics in the category
Strong style consistency controls
Fast iteration
cons: Public-by-default generation on lower tiers
No official API
No commercial indemnity comparable to Adobe's

stable-diffusion.name: Stable Diffusion
stable-diffusion.tagline: The open-weight image model that made local, private image generation possible.
stable-diffusion.value: Open-weight image generation that can run entirely on your own hardware. The only mainstream option where confidential visual work never leaves the building, and the base for most of the fine-tuning ecosystem.
use_cases: Generating imagery on confidential product or brand material locally
Fine-tuning a model on an organization's own visual style
High-volume generation without per-image cost
stable-diffusion.engine: Stability AI's open-weight diffusion models, in several generations and sizes.
stable-diffusion.files: Text prompts, image inputs, masks, and control inputs depending on the pipeline.
stable-diffusion.latency: Hardware dependent. Fast on a capable GPU, slow on CPU.
stable-diffusion.quality: Very good, and highly controllable through the surrounding tooling. Base output aesthetics generally trail Midjourney; controllability is far ahead.
stable-diffusion.training_optout: Self-hosted use means nothing leaves your infrastructure. Hosted use follows Stability's terms.
stable-diffusion.governance_note: Licensing is the thing to check, not capability. Stability's model licences have changed across releases and some carry revenue-linked commercial conditions, so the licence attached to the specific checkpoint matters more than the family name. Separately, the training-data provenance litigation affecting the category applies here too: self-hosting removes the data-exposure risk but not the copyright question about outputs.
integrations: The broad open ecosystem of interfaces and fine-tuning tools
stable-diffusion.api: REST API for the hosted service; locally, whatever pipeline you build.
pros: Fully self-hostable, nothing leaves your infrastructure
Unmatched controllability and fine-tuning ecosystem
No per-image cost when self-hosted
cons: Licence terms vary by release and need reading each time
Base aesthetics behind Midjourney
Requires real technical capability

adobe-firefly.name: Adobe Firefly
adobe-firefly.tagline: Image generation built for commercial use, with indemnity, which is the point.
adobe-firefly.value: Trained on licensed and public-domain material rather than an undisclosed web scrape, and sold with enterprise indemnity. For organizations where legal review gates creative tooling, that provenance position matters more than output quality.
use_cases: Commercial marketing imagery where provenance must survive legal review
Generative editing inside Photoshop and Illustrator workflows already in place
Brand-controlled generation using an organization's own approved assets
adobe-firefly.engine: Adobe's own Firefly models, positioned on licensed training data.
adobe-firefly.files: Text prompts and image inputs, with deep integration into Adobe file formats.
adobe-firefly.latency: Fast enough for interactive editing inside the Creative Cloud applications.
adobe-firefly.quality: Good, and improving, though generally behind Midjourney on pure aesthetics. Its advantage is integration and legal posture rather than raw output.
adobe-firefly.training_optout: Enterprise agreements cover customer content use. Adobe's position on training data provenance is the product's central claim and should be read directly rather than taken second-hand.
adobe-firefly.governance_note: This is the reference case for training-data provenance as a procurement criterion. Where a generator cannot say what it was trained on, the organization inherits that uncertainty on every asset it publishes. Firefly's commercial indemnity converts that uncertainty into a contractual allocation, which is exactly the sort of control an auditor can test. Content Credentials support also helps with the provenance-labelling obligations now appearing in AI law.
integrations: Photoshop, Illustrator, Express, and the wider Creative Cloud
adobe-firefly.api: Firefly Services API for enterprise automation.
pros: Licensed training data and commercial indemnity
Native inside existing Adobe workflows
Content Credentials support provenance labelling
cons: Aesthetics behind the leaders
Credit-based pricing is easy to exhaust
Best value assumes you already pay for Creative Cloud

otter-ai.name: Otter.ai
otter-ai.tagline: Meeting transcription and notes, and the tool most likely to create a consent problem.
otter-ai.value: Joins meetings, transcribes them, and produces searchable notes and summaries automatically. Removes note-taking overhead entirely, which is why adoption tends to spread through an organization without anyone approving it.
use_cases: Automatic transcripts and summaries of recurring internal meetings
Searchable archive of decisions across many calls
Accessibility, live captioning for participants who need it
otter-ai.engine: Proprietary speech recognition and summarisation models.
otter-ai.files: Live meeting audio plus uploaded audio and video files.
otter-ai.latency: Real-time captioning during the meeting; summaries follow shortly after.
otter-ai.quality: Strong on clear audio and standard accents. Degrades with crosstalk, heavy accents, and specialised vocabulary, and summaries occasionally attribute a statement to the wrong speaker, which matters more than a plain transcription error.
otter-ai.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers offer data controls. Consumer tiers differ. Verify before any privileged or regulated conversation is recorded.
otter-ai.governance_note: The highest-risk tool in ordinary daily use, and the risk is legal rather than technical. Recording consent law varies by jurisdiction: several US states require all-party consent, and recording a call without it is a criminal matter in some of them, not a policy breach. Add legal privilege, HR investigations, and regulated client conversations and the exposure compounds. Any deployment needs an explicit consent practice, a retention policy, and a clear list of meeting types where it must never join. This is also the tool most often found in an AI inventory that nobody approved.
otter-ai.api: API available on higher tiers for transcript retrieval and workflow integration.
pros: Removes meeting note-taking entirely
Strong searchable archive across many meetings
Live captioning aids accessibility
cons: Recording consent exposure is serious and jurisdiction-dependent
Speaker attribution errors carry real consequences
Spreads through organizations without approval

grammarly.name: Grammarly
grammarly.tagline: Writing assistance almost everyone already has installed, reading almost everything they type.
grammarly.value: Real-time correction and rewriting wherever text is typed, across browser, desktop, and mobile. Ubiquity is the product: it works everywhere without changing how anyone works.
use_cases: Correctness and tone consistency across all business writing
Enforcing a house style guide across a large team
Non-native English speakers producing publication-quality writing
grammarly.engine: Proprietary language models, with third-party frontier models behind some generative features.
grammarly.files: Operates on text in place. Document upload in the web editor.
grammarly.quality: Excellent on mechanics and clarity. Style suggestions can flatten distinctive voice if accepted uncritically.

pricing.includes: Style guide, SSO, admin analytics, data controls

grammarly.training_optout: Business and enterprise tiers carry stronger data commitments than the free tier. Verify which applies to the seats actually deployed.
grammarly.governance_note: The exposure here is breadth, not depth. A browser extension with permission to read and modify text sees drafts of everything: board material, legal correspondence, HR matters, client data, and anything typed into an internal system. It is frequently installed by individuals on the free tier and so never appears in a vendor review. Two practical controls: manage the extension through browser policy rather than leaving it to individuals, and confirm which tier the organization is actually running, because free and enterprise carry materially different terms.
grammarly.api: Limited. Primarily an end-user product rather than a platform.
pros: Works everywhere without workflow change
Genuinely effective on mechanics and clarity
Style guide enforcement at enterprise tier
cons: Extension sees an extremely broad slice of organizational text
Free-tier installs bypass vendor review entirely
Style suggestions can flatten voice

notion-ai.name: Notion AI
notion-ai.tagline: AI inside the workspace, answering from the company's own pages.
notion-ai.value: Writes, summarises, and answers questions against the organization's own Notion content, respecting existing page permissions. Most useful precisely where a company has already committed its documentation to Notion.
use_cases: Answering questions from internal documentation without hunting for the page
Drafting and summarising directly inside working documents
Turning meeting notes into structured, actionable records
notion-ai.engine: Third-party frontier models operating over Notion workspace content.
notion-ai.files: Workspace pages and databases, plus uploaded files and connected sources.
notion-ai.latency: Fast for in-page work; retrieval across a large workspace is slower.
notion-ai.quality: Good at summarising and drafting from source pages. Answer quality is bounded by documentation quality, so a messy workspace produces confident answers from stale pages.
notion-ai.training_optout: Notion states customer data is not used to train models. Because generation runs on third-party models, the sub-processor list is the thing to read, not just the headline commitment.
notion-ai.governance_note: Two points. First, it inherits Notion page permissions, so it will answer from anything the asking user can already open, which turns permissive workspace sharing into an information-disclosure route. Second, answers are only as current as the pages behind them: a superseded policy page will be quoted back with full confidence. Documentation hygiene becomes a control, not just housekeeping.
integrations: Connectors to common storage and communication tools
notion-ai.api: Notion API for workspace content; AI features are primarily in-product.
pros: Answers from the organization's own documented knowledge
No context switch out of the working document
Respects existing page permissions
cons: Only as good as the documentation behind it
Inherits permissive sharing as a disclosure path
Depends on third-party models, so read the sub-processor list

claude-code.name: Claude Code
claude-code.tagline: An agentic coding tool that works in the terminal against a whole repository.
claude-code.value: Operates on a repository the way a developer does: reads files, makes multi-file changes, runs commands, and iterates on the result. Suited to a described task rather than a completed line.
use_cases: Multi-file refactors and feature implementation from a written description
Investigating and fixing a bug across an unfamiliar codebase
Automating repetitive engineering work such as migrations and test scaffolding
claude-code.files: Whole-repository access within the directory it is run in, subject to its permission prompts.
claude-code.latency: Slower than inline completion by design, because it is reading, editing, and verifying rather than predicting the next token.
claude-code.quality: Strong on substantial multi-file changes. As with any agentic tool, a confident wrong change spread across several files is harder to spot in review than a single bad line.
claude-code.training_optout: Follows Anthropic's commercial terms: business and API data is not used for training by default.
claude-code.governance_note: Agentic coding tools change the control question from what the model reads to what it is allowed to do. It executes commands and edits files, so scope it deliberately: run it in a repository rather than a home directory, keep secrets out of the working tree, and require human review before merge. The corresponding audit evidence is the pull request history, which is where the record of what an agent changed actually lives.
integrations: Model Context Protocol for external systems
claude-code.api: Built on the Anthropic API; usage can be billed through it directly.
pros: Genuinely effective on whole-repository work
Fits existing terminal and Git workflow
Clear enterprise data terms
cons: Executes commands, so scoping and review discipline are mandatory
Usage costs escalate on large tasks
Confident multi-file errors are hard to catch in review

whisper-openai.name: Whisper API (OpenAI)
whisper-openai.tagline: Open-weight speech recognition, accurate enough that every other vendor benchmarks against it.
whisper-openai.value: The strongest freely available speech-to-text model, and the reference benchmark for the category. Available both as an OpenAI API and as open weights you can run yourself, which is an unusual combination at this quality level.
use_cases: Transcribing audio and video files at scale through the API
Self-hosting accurate speech recognition inside a controlled environment
Building voice interfaces or meeting-note pipelines on a reliable accuracy floor
whisper-openai.engine: OpenAI's Whisper model family, released as open weights. The API runs a hosted version.
whisper-openai.files: Audio and video files in common formats.
whisper-openai.latency: Not real-time in the base form. The OpenAI API is fast for file transcription; real-time streaming requires the Realtime API endpoint.
whisper-openai.quality: Best-in-class across languages and accents for an open-weight model. Still degrades on heavy background noise and very domain-specific vocabulary.

pricing.includes: Open weights, full control, no data sent to OpenAI

whisper-openai.training_optout: Self-hosted: nothing leaves your infrastructure. API: follows OpenAI's commercial data terms for the tier in use.
whisper-openai.governance_note: The self-hosted path is the right answer wherever the audio is privileged, regulated, or involves recording consent issues. An HR investigation interview, a legal call, or a clinical encounter should not be sent through an external API. Open weights mean you get the same model quality on your own infrastructure. Pair with an explicit retention policy for the resulting transcripts, which are often more sensitive than the audio.
integrations: Self-hosting via Hugging Face and common ML tooling
whisper-openai.api: REST API on OpenAI's platform. Open weights available for direct use.
pros: Best-in-class open-weight accuracy
Self-hosted path removes external data exposure
Wide language coverage
cons: Not real-time in the standard form
API cost accumulates at high audio volume
Transcripts inherit the sensitivity of the underlying conversation

llamaindex.name: LlamaIndex
llamaindex.tagline: The framework for building retrieval-augmented applications on top of your own documents.
llamaindex.value: The standard framework for connecting language models to private document stores. Where LangChain is more general-purpose, LlamaIndex is specifically optimized for the ingest-index-retrieve-generate pattern that makes RAG work well in practice.
use_cases: Building a knowledge assistant that answers questions from internal documents
Creating a retrieval layer that feeds context into a language model accurately
Ingesting heterogeneous sources (PDFs, databases, APIs) into a queryable index
llamaindex.engine: Framework, not a model. Orchestrates calls to whatever model and vector store you choose.
llamaindex.files: Loaders for PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, databases, and web pages.
llamaindex.latency: Framework overhead is minimal; latency is dominated by the model and vector store.
llamaindex.quality: Retrieval quality depends heavily on chunking strategy and embedding model choice. LlamaIndex provides the plumbing; the quality decisions sit with the implementer.
llamaindex.training_optout: Framework only. Data handling depends entirely on the model and store chosen.
llamaindex.governance_note: The governance surface of a RAG system is the index, not the model. Whatever documents go in can come out in model responses, including documents that were accessible to the indexing process but should not be surfaced to end users. Access control on the index is not automatic and must be designed explicitly. The most common failure is indexing a shared drive and discovering that everyone can now query everyone else's sensitive files.
integrations: Every major vector store and embedding provider
llamaindex.api: Python library, TypeScript available. Extensive integration surface.
pros: The right tool for document-centric RAG specifically
Excellent integration coverage
Strong community and documentation
cons: Index access control is not automatic
Configuration choices strongly affect retrieval quality
TypeScript support lags Python

runway.name: Runway
runway.tagline: The professional video generation and editing suite used in real production.
runway.value: The video AI tool with the most traction in professional film and commercial production. Not a toy generator but a production tool, with temporal consistency and control that distinguishes it from consumer video tools.
use_cases: Generating video from text or image references for commercial production
In-painting, out-painting, and background replacement in existing footage
Rapid iteration on video concepts before committing to live production
runway.engine: Runway's proprietary video generation models (Gen series).
runway.files: Text prompts, image references, and existing video clips for editing and extension.
runway.latency: Generation takes minutes for longer clips. Fast enough for iterative creative work, not for real-time use.
runway.quality: The quality leader for temporal consistency and cinematic control among commercial video generators.

pricing.includes: Generation credits, watermark removal on higher tiers
Indemnity, private hosting, SSO, admin controls

runway.training_optout: Enterprise terms address training use of customer content. Consumer tiers differ. Check before submitting proprietary production assets.
runway.governance_note: The same synthetic-likeness and training-provenance issues that apply to image generators apply here, compounded by video's ability to portray motion and speech. Using an identifiable person's likeness in generated video without consent is the clearest exposure: several jurisdictions regulate it, and the area is moving fast. The enterprise indemnity offering is the tier to evaluate where commercial publication is the end state.
integrations: API for integration into production pipelines
runway.api: REST API with SDKs for integrating generation into larger workflows.
pros: Best-in-class temporal consistency and cinematic control
Enterprise tier with indemnity
Used in actual professional production
cons: Expensive at production volume
Synthetic likeness exposure is real and rising
Consumer tiers lack the data controls enterprises need

perplexity-enterprise.name: Perplexity Enterprise Pro
perplexity-enterprise.tagline: The enterprise tier of the citing answer engine, with data controls and SSO.
perplexity-enterprise.value: Extends the Perplexity citing-answer model to enterprise requirements: SSO, admin controls, data retention controls, and prompts not used for training. The underlying product is the same, with the security envelope that regulated organizations need.
use_cases: Organization-wide research capability with audit and admin oversight
Replacing ad-hoc web research with a citable, policy-compliant tool
Embedding sourced answers in internal workflows via the API
perplexity-enterprise.engine: Same as Perplexity AI: multi-model retrieval-augmented generation with citations.
perplexity-enterprise.files: Web retrieval plus document uploads where supported.
perplexity-enterprise.quality: Same quality characteristics as the consumer product. Citations require the same read-the-source discipline.

pricing.includes: SSO, admin controls, data retention controls, no training opt-in

perplexity-enterprise.training_optout: Enterprise Pro explicitly excludes customer data from model training. Verify the current contract terms.
perplexity-enterprise.governance_note: Same evidentiary point as the consumer product, now under admin control. The admin dashboard tells you which seats are active and what the usage looks like, which matters for the AI inventory. Citations are still leads, not evidence, and that rule does not change with the tier.
pros: Consumer product quality with enterprise data controls
Admin dashboard for inventory and governance
Data training opt-out by default
cons: Citations still require verification
Per-seat annual pricing can be hard to size ahead of adoption
Relies on web retrieval quality

grammarly-education.name: Grammarly for Education
grammarly-education.tagline: The campus licence of Grammarly, and the centre of the academic integrity debate.
grammarly-education.value: Writing assistance deployed at institutional scale across students and staff, with campus admin controls and reporting. The product itself is the same as the business edition; the conversation around it is not.
use_cases: Improving student writing clarity and mechanics at scale
Identifying writing patterns across the student body through admin analytics
Non-native English speakers developing academic writing competence
grammarly-education.engine: Same as Grammarly. Proprietary models, some generative features on third-party models.
grammarly-education.files: Text in place, in browsers and editors.
grammarly-education.training_optout: Institutional terms address data use. Confirm which terms apply to the specific agreement, not the product marketing.
grammarly-education.governance_note: The governance question in education is not the product, it is the policy. Grammarly corrects grammar; the moment its generative features write sentences, the academic integrity question is live. Institutions need a clear published policy on which features are within-bounds and which are not, before deploying a campus licence rather than after the first academic misconduct case. The admin analytics also surface usage patterns that have FERPA implications if the data is not handled as an education record.
integrations: Learning management system connectors on some tiers
pros: Meaningful help at scale for non-native English writers
Admin oversight not available on consumer tier
Proven at large institutional deployments
cons: Generative features blur the academic integrity line without an explicit policy
Admin analytics carry FERPA handling requirements
Free consumer installs can coexist with the campus licence and bypass controls

mistral-large.name: Mistral Large 2
mistral-large.tagline: Mistral's frontier model, the one in the proprietary tier, not the open-weight releases.
mistral-large.value: Mistral's strongest model, aimed at the tasks where the smaller open-weight models fall short: complex reasoning, long-document analysis, and demanding coding work. Retains the EU-residency argument of the Mistral family.
use_cases: Demanding reasoning and analysis requiring frontier capability under EU data terms
Enterprise API deployment where EU residency is required and quality cannot be compromised
Tasks where Mistral's lighter models show limits
mistral-large.engine: Mistral's proprietary frontier model. Not open weight.
mistral-large.files: Document and image handling via the API.
mistral-large.quality: Frontier-class. Competitive on reasoning and coding benchmarks with the US majors.
mistral-large.training_optout: API and enterprise terms address training data use. Verify for your tier.
mistral-large.governance_note: The EU-residency distinction that makes Mistral / Le Chat interesting applies equally here. The difference from the open-weight models is that this one cannot be self-hosted, so the data path runs through Mistral's infrastructure. That is still a significantly simpler transfer analysis than a US provider for a European organization, but it is not the same as self-hosting an Apache-licensed weight.
pros: Frontier quality under EU data terms
Simpler GDPR transfer analysis than US providers for EU organizations
Competitive pricing at the API tier
cons: Not self-hostable, unlike the open-weight models
Smaller ecosystem than the US majors
Less third-party tooling and documentation

zapier-ai.name: Zapier AI
zapier-ai.tagline: AI layered on top of Zapier's automation network: 7,000 apps, text inputs, no code.
zapier-ai.value: Adds text-driven automation and AI actions to the workflows most organizations already run in Zapier. The value is the integration surface, 7,000-plus apps, not any particular model capability.
use_cases: Building AI-powered automations across SaaS tools without code
Routing, classifying, and acting on incoming data through natural language steps
Connecting AI outputs to downstream systems without building custom integrations
zapier-ai.engine: Routes to third-party models (primarily OpenAI) through Zapier's action layer.
zapier-ai.files: Handles the data formats and payloads of the connected apps.
zapier-ai.latency: Async by nature, suited to background automation rather than interactive use.
zapier-ai.quality: Quality of the AI step depends on the underlying model. Value is in the connectivity, not the model.

pricing.model: Per-task pricing within existing Zapier pricing

zapier-ai.training_optout: Follows OpenAI and any other sub-processor's terms for the model step. Zapier itself operates under its own data terms. Both matter.
zapier-ai.governance_note: Automation tools have a specific failure mode: they keep running when the world changes. An AI automation approved in one context will continue executing months later when the data, the counterparties, or the policy have shifted. Human review checkpoints must be designed in from the start, not added when something goes wrong. The audit question is not whether the automation worked today but whether anyone would know if it stopped working correctly.
zapier-ai.api: Zapier API for programmatic Zap management.
pros: Unmatched integration surface
No-code AI automation accessible to non-developers
Existing Zapier workflows gain AI steps without rebuilding
cons: Automation continues running when context changes
Sub-processor chain for the model step needs tracking
Quality depends on the model behind the AI step

zapier-central.name: Zapier Central
zapier-central.tagline: Zapier's agent layer: bots that observe and act across your connected apps.
zapier-central.value: Persistent AI agents that watch for conditions in connected apps and take actions when those conditions are met. Where Zapier AI is a step in a Zap, Central is a standing agent with memory and multi-step reasoning.
use_cases: Monitoring inboxes, CRMs, and ticketing systems and acting when conditions are met
Cross-app workflows that require conditional logic beyond simple if-this-then-that
Delegating recurring multi-step operational tasks to a managed agent
zapier-central.engine: Routes to frontier models via Zapier's infrastructure over the same app network.
zapier-central.latency: Async. Agents run on a schedule or on trigger.
zapier-central.quality: As an agentic product, output quality depends on prompt quality and how well edge cases are handled in the agent's instructions.
zapier-central.training_optout: Same sub-processor chain as Zapier AI. Review both Zapier's terms and the underlying model provider's.
zapier-central.governance_note: An agent that runs autonomously across your business data is a materially different risk profile from a one-shot automation. Two controls are essential: a minimum-permission posture (the agent should connect to only the apps and data it genuinely needs), and a clear escalation path for edge cases the agent encounters. The most common failure pattern is an agent handling an edge case by making a plausible-but-wrong decision, and no one noticing until the downstream consequence has propagated.
zapier-central.api: In development; primarily a UI-driven product.
pros: Standing agents over a vast integration network
No-code agent configuration
Memory and multi-step reasoning
cons: Autonomous action at scale requires deliberate scoping
Sub-processor chain must be tracked
Edge-case handling requires human escalation design

ibm-openscale.name: IBM watsonx.governance
ibm-openscale.tagline: IBM's enterprise AI governance platform: model monitoring, explainability, and audit.
ibm-openscale.value: The most established enterprise governance platform from a traditional software vendor. Covers model monitoring, drift detection, fairness testing, and audit-trail generation across both IBM and third-party models. Sold to regulated industries on the strength of its on-premises deployment option and IBM's compliance track record.
use_cases: Monitoring production ML models for drift, bias, and performance degradation
Generating explainability artifacts for regulator inquiries
Building a governed model lifecycle from training through retirement
ibm-openscale.engine: Monitors models from any provider. Runs its own explainability and fairness algorithms.
ibm-openscale.files: Integrates with model stores, feature stores, and data warehouses.
ibm-openscale.latency: Background monitoring, not interactive. Dashboards update periodically.
ibm-openscale.quality: Deep and auditable. Configuration complexity is real, and the investment in setup is proportional to the environment it is managing.

pricing.includes: Managed deployment, monitoring, and explainability features

ibm-openscale.training_optout: On-premises deployment means model and data stay on your infrastructure. Cloud deployment follows IBM's standard data terms.
ibm-openscale.governance_note: This is what an AI audit of a regulated organization's model estate looks like in practice: continuous monitoring, explainability, and documented evidence rather than a point-in-time review. The EU AI Act's high-risk system requirements (Article 9 risk management, Article 17 quality management) describe exactly this kind of ongoing oversight. The product is expensive and complex, and the right question is whether your model estate is large enough to justify it, or whether lighter tooling covers the actual scope.
integrations: IBM Watson Studio and the wider IBM data and AI stack
Enterprise data warehouses and feature stores
ibm-openscale.api: REST APIs for monitoring and metadata. SDK for integration.
pros: Deepest governance feature set in the category
On-premises option removes cloud data exposure
IBM's regulated-industry track record
cons: Significant configuration and implementation investment
Best value inside an existing IBM stack
Complexity may exceed needs of smaller model estates

arize-ai.name: Arize AI
arize-ai.tagline: Model observability for ML and LLM applications, used by ML teams already in production.
arize-ai.value: The practical choice for an ML team that needs model observability without the full enterprise governance stack. Handles traditional ML monitoring (drift, performance) and LLM tracing, evaluation, and prompt monitoring in one platform.
use_cases: Monitoring deployed ML and LLM applications for performance and data drift
Tracing LLM applications to debug prompt failures and quality issues
Running automated evaluations on LLM outputs in CI/CD
arize-ai.engine: Monitoring platform, not a model. Connects to model outputs and feature data.
arize-ai.files: Accepts prediction logs, embeddings, and LLM traces.
arize-ai.quality: Strong on LLM tracing and evaluation, which is an area most governance platforms added late. Good ML monitoring depth.
arize-ai.training_optout: Monitoring platform, not a model host. Data retention and use terms govern what Arize stores from your prediction logs.
arize-ai.governance_note: LLM observability is the gap in most organizations' AI risk management: they monitor traditional ML models and then deploy LLM applications with no production visibility at all. A hallucination rate, a prompt injection, or a quality regression in an LLM feature is invisible without tracing. The audit question to ask is which deployed AI features have monitoring, and which are running dark.
integrations: Most ML frameworks and serving platforms
LangChain, LlamaIndex, and LLM orchestration tools
CI/CD pipelines for eval in deployment
pros: Strong LLM tracing alongside traditional ML monitoring
Practical tool built by practitioners
Good CI/CD integration for eval
cons: SaaS means prediction data leaves your infrastructure
Pricing can scale fast at high volume
Less enterprise compliance depth than IBM's offering

harvey-ai.name: Harvey AI
harvey-ai.tagline: AI for legal work, built specifically for law firms and legal departments.
harvey-ai.value: Legal-domain AI built for law firms rather than adapted from a general assistant. Handles legal research, document drafting, contract review, and due diligence in the contexts a lawyer actually works in, not the contexts a general AI was trained on.
use_cases: Legal research and issue spotting across case law and statutes
First-pass contract review and redlining
Due diligence document review at scale
harvey-ai.engine: Built on frontier models (primarily OpenAI and Anthropic) with legal-domain fine-tuning and retrieval.
harvey-ai.files: Legal documents: contracts, filings, case documents, and statutory text.
harvey-ai.latency: Fast enough for interactive research. Document review at scale is batch.
harvey-ai.quality: Strongest for legal English and legal reasoning. Outputs still require lawyer review before any client-facing use.

pricing.includes: Data controls, professional liability alignment, admin oversight

harvey-ai.training_optout: Legal-grade data terms. Client matter data is not used to train models. Verify the DPA for your jurisdiction.
harvey-ai.governance_note: The legal professional responsibility question is the same regardless of tool: a lawyer cannot delegate judgment to an AI, and outputs must be reviewed before they touch client work. What changes is which tasks can be accelerated. The professional liability point is that if Harvey produces a flawed contract clause and a lawyer submits it without review, the lawyer's error, not the vendor's. On the data side, privilege must be maintained for client matter inputs, which requires a confirmed data path under the firm's privilege policy, not just the vendor's standard terms.
integrations: Document management systems used in legal practice
pros: Legal-domain specificity rather than general adaptation
Data terms designed for client matter sensitivity
Meaningful research and review acceleration
cons: Lawyer review remains mandatory before any client-facing use
Privilege policy must be confirmed for the specific data path
Enterprise-only pricing, no self-serve access

casetext-cocounsel.name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
casetext-cocounsel.tagline: Legal AI from Thomson Reuters, strongest on US caselaw and legal research.
casetext-cocounsel.value: AI legal research and document analysis from Casetext, now part of Thomson Reuters. Deep integration with Westlaw and a long track record in US legal research distinguish it from newer entrants.
use_cases: US caselaw research and citation checking
Deposition preparation and key issue extraction from document productions
Contract analysis and quick-turn research memos
casetext-cocounsel.engine: Built on GPT-4 with legal-domain fine-tuning and Westlaw retrieval.
casetext-cocounsel.files: Legal documents, contracts, deposition transcripts, and production sets.
casetext-cocounsel.quality: Strongest on US common law. The Thomson Reuters integration gives it a sourcing depth other tools lack. Still requires lawyer review.
casetext-cocounsel.training_optout: Thomson Reuters / Casetext terms govern customer data use. Verify under the current agreement.
casetext-cocounsel.governance_note: Same professional responsibility framing as Harvey: the tool accelerates, the lawyer is still accountable. The Westlaw integration is specifically valuable for the sourcing chain, because a hallucinated citation is immediately checkable rather than requiring a separate lookup. Attorney-client privilege analysis for the data path applies as with any legal AI.
pros: Deep Westlaw integration for US law
Established trust record in law firms
Thomson Reuters data governance backing
cons: US caselaw focus limits international utility
Lawyer review still mandatory
Less generalist than Harvey for corporate transactional work

azure-openai.name: Azure OpenAI Service
azure-openai.tagline: OpenAI's models running in Azure, under Microsoft's enterprise data terms.
azure-openai.value: The OpenAI model family (GPT, Embeddings, Whisper, DALL-E) deployed inside Azure's infrastructure, under Azure's enterprise data terms, IAM, networking, and compliance controls. For organizations already on Azure, this is the path to OpenAI capabilities without the consumer data-handling question.
use_cases: Enterprise AI applications where data must stay inside an existing Azure tenancy
Standardizing the organization on one model API with consistent billing and controls
Regulated industries requiring regional data residency and VNET integration
azure-openai.engine: OpenAI models: GPT series, embeddings, Whisper, DALL-E, deployed on Azure infrastructure.
azure-openai.files: Same as the OpenAI API; the difference is where it runs.
azure-openai.quality: Identical to OpenAI's models. The differentiation is the deployment environment.

pricing.includes: Same models as OpenAI API under Azure billing

azure-openai.training_optout: Microsoft's commercial data terms apply: Azure OpenAI does not use customer data to train models. This is the point. Verify via the Microsoft Product Terms, not the OpenAI terms, which do not govern here.
azure-openai.governance_note: The governance case is simple: it is the same capability as the OpenAI API under Microsoft's enterprise compliance envelope. For organizations that have already approved Azure for sensitive data, this is usually the faster path to deployment than a separate OpenAI vendor review. The specific controls to confirm are VNET integration, private endpoints, and whether the region chosen satisfies any data residency requirements. One common mistake is deploying to a convenient region without checking residency.
integrations: Full Azure service ecosystem: Cognitive Search, Azure AI Foundry, VNET, Log Analytics
Enterprise identity and access via Azure AD
Same SDK surface as the OpenAI API
azure-openai.api: OpenAI-compatible REST API plus Azure SDK. Same client libraries work with a base-URL change.
pros: Enterprise data terms, not consumer terms
Azure compliance controls (residency, VNET, private endpoints)
Same models as OpenAI API, unified billing
cons: Regional availability lags OpenAI's model releases
Quota allocation requires a separate approval process
Adds Azure dependency for teams not already on the platform

google-vertex-ai.name: Google Vertex AI
google-vertex-ai.tagline: Google's enterprise AI platform: model deployment, MLOps, and Gemini under GCP controls.
google-vertex-ai.value: Google's unified ML platform for training, deployment, and management, with Gemini and third-party models available under GCP's enterprise controls. The enterprise answer when the organization is already on GCP and needs both the Gemini family and ML platform capabilities in one place.
use_cases: Deploying and managing ML and generative AI at enterprise scale under GCP
Accessing Gemini models with GCP's IAM, VNET, and residency controls
Building end-to-end ML pipelines with managed training, evaluation, and serving
google-vertex-ai.engine: Gemini model family plus third-party and open-source models available through Model Garden.
google-vertex-ai.files: Training data, models, and inference payloads in GCP storage formats.
google-vertex-ai.latency: Comparable to other cloud model endpoints.
google-vertex-ai.quality: Gemini models under GCP controls. Same quality characteristics, different data terms.
google-vertex-ai.training_optout: GCP enterprise terms: customer data is not used to train Google's models. Verify via the GCP Data Processing Amendment.
google-vertex-ai.governance_note: Same data-path logic as Azure OpenAI: enterprise controls convert a consumer data-handling question into an enterprise compliance question. Residency and VNET are the controls to confirm. Model Garden also surfaces third-party and open-source models with their own licences, so licence review applies to those selections even though they are accessed through a managed platform.
integrations: Full GCP ecosystem: BigQuery, Cloud Storage, IAM, VNET
Vertex AI Workbench, Pipelines, and Feature Store
Same Gemini API surface as the developer product
google-vertex-ai.api: REST API and Google Cloud SDK.
pros: Gemini family under enterprise GCP controls
End-to-end ML platform in one place
GCP residency and IAM controls for regulated industries
cons: Best value assumes GCP commitment
Platform complexity requires MLOps capability
Third-party model licences need independent review

crowdstrike-charlotte.name: CrowdStrike Charlotte AI
crowdstrike-charlotte.tagline: AI across the CrowdStrike Falcon platform, answering security questions in natural language.
crowdstrike-charlotte.value: Natural language access to the CrowdStrike Falcon telemetry: ask in English, get an answer grounded in your organization's own security data. Reduces the query burden on analysts and surfaces context that would otherwise require a specialist to retrieve.
use_cases: Asking natural language questions against the organization's security telemetry
Summarising incidents and threat context for analysts under pressure
Accelerating triage by surfacing relevant context without manual hunting
crowdstrike-charlotte.engine: Frontier models grounded on CrowdStrike Falcon telemetry and threat intelligence.
crowdstrike-charlotte.files: Falcon platform telemetry: endpoint, identity, cloud, and network data.
crowdstrike-charlotte.latency: Interactive for queries. Continuous monitoring is background.
crowdstrike-charlotte.quality: Bounded by the quality and coverage of your Falcon deployment. Better data coverage produces better answers.

pricing.includes: Charlotte AI features across licensed Falcon modules

crowdstrike-charlotte.training_optout: CrowdStrike's terms govern customer data use. Grounding on your own telemetry is the architectural pattern; verify the data retention and training terms in the customer agreement.
crowdstrike-charlotte.governance_note: Security AI tools create an audit question that general AI tools do not: if the AI missed something, was it because the telemetry was incomplete, the model missed it, or the analyst did not ask the right question? Documenting which AI-assisted decisions were made and what they were grounded on matters for incident response and for regulator inquiries in sectors with notification obligations. The AI layer is not a substitute for human judgment on significant incidents; it is a retrieval accelerator.
integrations: Deeply embedded in the Falcon platform
crowdstrike-charlotte.api: Falcon API with Charlotte AI capabilities.
pros: Grounded on your organization's own security data
Natural language dramatically lowers analyst query friction
No data leaves the Falcon platform boundary
cons: Only useful if already running Falcon
Answer quality is limited by telemetry coverage
AI-assisted decisions still require human review for significant events

darktrace.name: Darktrace
darktrace.tagline: Autonomous cyber AI that detects and responds to threats by learning normal behaviour.
darktrace.value: Network and endpoint security that builds a model of normal behaviour for every device and user, then detects and responds to deviations autonomously. The autonomous-response capability is both the product's main differentiator and the clearest governance challenge.
use_cases: Detecting novel attacks that signature-based tools miss
Autonomous containment of active threats without waiting for analyst action
Continuous monitoring across network, cloud, email, and identity
darktrace.engine: Proprietary unsupervised machine learning. Not an LLM product; it learns patterns rather than reasoning in language.
darktrace.files: Network traffic, endpoint telemetry, email, cloud, and identity logs.
darktrace.latency: Continuous real-time monitoring. Autonomous response triggers within seconds.
darktrace.quality: Sensitive detection across subtle behavioural deviation. False positive rate management is the primary implementation challenge.
darktrace.training_optout: The model learns your environment. Darktrace's terms govern what they retain. Autonomous action is taken on your infrastructure, which is the salient governance point.
darktrace.governance_note: Autonomous response is where AI governance and security governance converge. Darktrace can act: it can isolate a device, block a connection, or quarantine a user account without human approval, in seconds. That capability prevents damage, and it also carries risk if a false positive triggers it on a critical system during peak hours. The governance requirement is explicit policy on which autonomous actions are approved, under which conditions, with what notification, and who has the authority to override. Those decisions belong in a human-reviewed policy document, not in the tool's default settings.
darktrace.api: Darktrace API for SIEM integration and management.
pros: Detects novel threats that rules miss
Sub-second autonomous response
Broad coverage across network, cloud, and identity
cons: Autonomous action requires explicit policy governance
False positive management is ongoing work
Premium pricing

glean.name: Glean
glean.tagline: Enterprise search that connects every SaaS tool and answers from your own content.
glean.value: Unified search across an organization's entire SaaS stack, with a knowledge assistant that answers from the real content rather than generic training data. Particularly valuable in organizations where institutional knowledge is fragmented across many tools.
use_cases: Finding anything across Slack, email, Confluence, Jira, Drive, and 100+ other sources
Answering questions from internal documentation without knowing where it lives
Reducing time spent finding information as a recurring daily tax
glean.engine: Proprietary retrieval models plus frontier LLMs for answer generation, grounded on company content.
glean.files: Connects to and indexes SaaS tools via read-only connectors.
glean.latency: Search is near-instant. Generated answers take a few seconds.
glean.quality: Strong when the source content is well-maintained. As with all RAG systems, the answers are only as current as the indexed content.

pricing.includes: All connectors, AI assistant, admin controls

glean.training_optout: Glean does not train its models on customer content. The data stays indexed in a dedicated tenant. Verify the current DPA.
glean.governance_note: The information-disclosure risk from Glean runs in the same direction as with Microsoft Copilot and Notion AI: it surfaces content the user already has permission to see, but it surfaces it faster and in response to natural language questions. If permission settings are permissive, previously obscure content becomes easily discoverable. Run a permission audit on the connected sources before deploying rather than after discovering that an AI answered a question with a confidential document the user technically had access to.
pros: Genuinely useful for organizations with fragmented knowledge
Respects existing permissions from connected systems
Broad connector coverage
cons: Permissive legacy permissions become easily discoverable
Per-seat enterprise pricing at scale
Answer quality depends on documentation quality

devin-cognition.name: Devin (Cognition)
devin-cognition.tagline: The first commercially available AI software engineer, with its own computer.
devin-cognition.value: An agent that operates like a developer: it has its own browser, terminal, and code editor, receives a task description, and works through it with minimal handholding. Positioned at longer-horizon autonomous engineering rather than inline assistance.
use_cases: Autonomous feature development from a brief to a pull request
Bug investigation and fix across an unfamiliar codebase
Repetitive engineering tasks such as migrations and test generation at scale
devin-cognition.engine: Cognition's own model trained specifically for software engineering.
devin-cognition.files: Full repository access within its sandboxed environment.
devin-cognition.latency: Hours for substantial tasks. Not an interactive tool.
devin-cognition.quality: Capable on well-defined tasks with clear success criteria. Less reliable on ambiguous requirements or highly context-dependent design decisions.

pricing.includes: Task completion, PR generation, repository access

devin-cognition.training_optout: Verify data terms before giving repository access containing sensitive code.
devin-cognition.governance_note: This tool makes the agentic governance question concrete: an AI that can commit code, open PRs, and execute commands at the repository level is performing actions with consequences that outlast the session. Three controls are not optional: branch and PR policies that prevent direct commits to main, mandatory human code review before merge, and secrets management that ensures credentials are never in the repository Devin can access. The audit evidence is the git history. If you cannot reconstruct what an agent changed and why, you do not have a defensible record.
integrations: Standard developer tooling via its sandboxed environment
pros: Genuine autonomous long-horizon engineering capability
Full development environment under the agent's control
Clear PR-based output for human review
cons: Requires branch protection and mandatory review to be safe
Less reliable on ambiguous or design-heavy tasks
Data terms require careful review before repository access

canva-ai.name: Canva AI
canva-ai.tagline: AI design features embedded in the tool most marketing and operations teams already use.
canva-ai.value: AI-powered image generation, background removal, text effects, and presentation assistance inside the design tool most non-designer teams already use. The value is accessibility rather than frontier quality.
use_cases: Generating images and backgrounds for marketing collateral without a designer
Expanding, removing, or replacing image backgrounds in existing assets
